elements.August 1950: . At nine months old, I was found in my crib by my nanny, Alice. I was turning blue from not breathing. Alice wrapped me in a blanket and ran with me to the nearest main road in hopes of finding help. There were no phones on our farm at that time. She ran over a mile to the Farmer’s Store where Mr. Owen Farmer had just opened the General Store. She begged Mr. Farmer for assistance as she feared I was dead. He immediately drove us to the hospital. A German Doctor was in the emergency room teaching students about the newly developed drug, epinephrine, that was being used for severe anaphylactic shock. He took control of the situation. Epinephrine had not been used on a child, especially one as young as nine months old. I was revived. The doctor wrote up a case study that was published in a Medical Journal in 1950.
